free_tier.stated: Free plan: 10 MB maximum per attachment, 100 MB of attachments per 24 hours, up to 500 MB per 28 days. Premium: 100 MB per attachment, 1 GB/24h, 5 GB/28d. Accounts not on any plan get 500 MB/24h up to 2 GB/28d. So the total is a few GB per month. Not a storage provider at all.
free_tier.notes: Headline offer; binding constraint specified in limits.

per_object_cap.stated: No per-object cap documented in published terms; absence is not an unlimited claim.
per_object_cap.notes: extraction found no per-object clause; some of these providers meter on object count rather than bytes, and some state no cap

retention.stated: No retention statement documented in published terms; absence is not an unlimited claim.
retention.notes: No retention clause documented in available terms.

egress.terms: Egress itself is free ('the HTTPS data transfer to/from the matrix.org homeserver' does not count towards limits), but that is irrelevant at a 500 MB/28-day ingest rate.

tooling: Excellent. The Content Repository API is a real spec, mxc:// URIs, every Matrix client library implements it. Self-hosted Synapse has no such caps (only max_upload_size, default 10M historically).
chaining: Any federation of homeservers multiplies it, but you are then running the homeservers yourself, which is just 'buy a server'. On the public homeserver there is no chaining path: limits are per-account and the 28-day cap is the binding one.
limits_note: Unauthenticated media download is deprecated and already frozen: the spec says servers SHOULD 'freeze' the old /_matrix/media/* endpoints so post-freeze uploads are only reachable via authenticated endpoints. Probed: matrix.org /_matrix/client/v1/media/config -> 401 M_MISSING_TOKEN, unauthenticated /_matrix/media/v3/download/... -> 404. So no anonymous CDN reads.
